case.summary: The alert was triggered by a monitor sweep that identified a rare device profile (GT-I9060M Build/KTU84P | | chrome 65.0 for android) used for a $58.38 online purchase on card C09588-K1. The strongest fraud indicators are that this device has been seen on only ten cards ever but was used on nine other cards within 30 days, with seven of those transactions matching the amount within 2%, a pattern that is 10.7 times more common in confirmed fraud, and the customer denied making the purchase and still possesses the card; the strongest legit indicator is a model risk score of 0.32, which historically corresponds to a 14% fraud rate for product C transactions, and the purchaser's email domain (gmail.com) matches the card's usual usage. The case is judged fraud with a probability of 0.96. The recommended actions are to block the card, create a new case, file a report, and monitor the connected cards.

sar.narrative: This report concerns customer C09588, card C09588-K1, issued as a visa credit. On 2016-11-06, 1 transaction(s) totalling $58.38 were identified as part of one fraud episode, beginning with transaction 3436636. The activity took place online, product code(s) C, from device profile(s) GT-I9060M Build/KTU84P |  | chrome 65.0 for android | . The transactions were purchases from one device profile used across several customers' cards. The activity is assessed as card-not-present fraud: Rare device profile GT-I9060M Build/KTU84P |  | chrome 65.0 for android |  (10 cards ever) was used on 9 other cards within 30 days, 7 of them for amounts within 2% of this $58.38 purchase (in the closed months this shape was 10.7 times more common in confirmed fraud than in normal online traffic); Customer denied the transaction(s) when asked: Customer states they did not make this purchase and still has the card. The same device profile GT-I9060M Build/KTU84P |  | chrome 65.0 for android |  links this activity to 9 other card(s), including C00294-K2, C01002-K1, C04125-K2, C05307-K2, which indicates a common actor across cardholders. Earlier confirmed cases CC-3778, CC-4917, CC-4991 show the same pattern. When contacted, the cardholder stated they did not make the transaction(s), did not share the card details, and still has the card. The bank has recommended BLOCK_CARD, MONITOR_CONNECTED_CARDS and opened an internal case; the report is filed under R6, §3a.
